definitions.explanation: Describes someone or something that inspires warm affection through their cuteness or innocence. Stronger and more heartfelt than かわいい, often implying a desire to cherish or protect.

examples.japanese: ⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{愛|あい}くるしい⟦{笑顔|えがお}→笑顔：01884_egao⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{癒|いや}された→癒す：13616_iyasu⟧。
examples.english: I was comforted by the baby's adorable smile.

examples.japanese: {子猫|こねこ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{愛|あい}くるしい⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦こちら→こちら：00960_kochira⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つめていた→見つめる：04571_mitsumeru⟧。
examples.english: The kitten was gazing at me with its charming eyes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{幼|おさな}い→幼い：02337_osanai⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧たち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{愛|あい}くるしい⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{歌|うた}→歌：02179_uta⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歌|うた}っている→歌う：00684_utau⟧⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}て→見る：00283_miru⟧、⟦{思|おも}わ→思う：00492_omou⟧ず⟦{微笑|ほほえ}んだ→微笑む：02416_hohoemu⟧。
examples.english: I couldn't help smiling when I saw the little children singing in their sweet voices.

notes:
USAGE:
A literary, slightly elevated alternative to ⟦かわいい→かわいい：00857_kawaii⟧. Most often used to describe babies, small children, and baby animals. Less commonly used for adults. Appears more in written language and narration than in casual speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {愛|あい}くるしい⟦{笑顔|えがお}→笑顔：01884_egao⟧ (adorable smile)
- {愛|あい}くるしい⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧ (charming eyes)
- {愛|あい}くるしい⟦{仕草|しぐさ}→仕草：10917_shigusa⟧ (endearing gestures)
- {愛|あい}くるしい⟦{表情|ひょうじょう}→表情：03585_hyoujou⟧ (sweet expression)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦かわいい→かわいい：00857_kawaii⟧: cute — the general, everyday word for cuteness; broader in usage
- ⟦{愛|あい}らしい→愛らしい：12682_airashii⟧: lovely, charming — similar to {愛|あい}くるしい but slightly more refined and elegant
